- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing gradual mean reversion.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes in history; model reacts too aggressively.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecast mean is typically 2–4% higher than true mean; adjust downward by 1–2% for 30-day forecasts.
- Avoid overreacting to recent high prices; reduce forecast sensitivity to last 5–7 days.
- If history shows a recent downward trend, model should not overcorrect upward.
- Use a 3–5 day lag to smooth out short-term volatility before forecasting.
- For price spikes, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- Apply a downward bias correction for the last 10–15 days of the forecast, especially if true prices are trending lower.
